title: Final residual abstention triage — 2026-10-25

exactHeadVerification.scope: 1,258 Node tests passed; browser integration/build, system/browser/Python regression/data integrity, strict corpus/master-table generation, Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 tests, wheel build and clean wheel install passed. Live NIKL inventory remains skipped by configuration.

basis.note: The earlier 45-case count belongs to an earlier commit. This register describes the five remaining linguistic cases after source-backed rule licenses and the variant-aware 못잃어 entry. CI success verifies implementation and build contracts, not independent phonetic correctness.

externalTextSearch.scope: Targeted public text-page searches; PDF/audio sources were excluded from evidence review. A PDF result surfaced in general search output but was not opened or used.
externalTextSearch.outcome: Official cultural source supports the existence/category of 칭칭이소리; authoritative Korean-language descriptions support that interjections and fillers are a valid general category. No exact-form evidence resolves the remaining uncertainty.

policy: Do not clear strict-mode abstention by silently correcting source spelling.
Official Hangul pronunciation notation is not IPA gold.
A spelling candidate is not a pronunciation result; a candidate IPA is not an accepted Ukrainian target.
Keep unresolved when lexical identity, morphology, user intent, or independent IPA evidence is missing.
The source-/candidate-blind reviewer packets are a workflow artifact; blank submissions are not reviews.

Preserve exact source orthography for transcription: never silently replace a typo with a spelling candidate. If the author-designed engine can produce a rule-derived IPA string from the written form, expose it as diagnostic/provisional IPA even when unresolved morphology blocks accepted pronunciation or Ukrainian output.

cases.observedIssue: The token's lexical identity and morpheme boundary remain unknown. A source-index snippet labels a folk-song heading 칡칡이, but the extracted PDF text layer at [철마면 민요 26] reads 칭칭이 and gives the refrain 치기타 칭칭나네.

evidenceReviewed.claim: The opened PDF text layer at lines 20611–20622 reads [철마면 민요 26] 칡칡이, identifies singer 이문춘 (male, born 1923), fieldwork date 1991-10-19 and location 철마면 이곡리, and cites 이소라, 양산의 민요 (1992), p. 180. The refrain includes 치기타 칭칭나네.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Directly confirms the exact song heading and source metadata, but not its spoken realization. The text transcription alone does not establish whether 칡칡이 is a lexicalized title, a regional variant, or an editorial/transcription form; no audio/field notes were available.

evidenceReviewed.claim: The National Gugak Center encyclopedia entry for 칭칭이소리 lists 칭칭이 among the song's alternate names and describes it as a folk song associated with Gyeongsang-do.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Independent text-only contextual evidence that 칭칭이 is a real folk-song label; it does not establish that the isolated input 칡칡이 refers to this song or verify the disputed source heading.

cases.productionChange: No production rule or accepted IPA. Keep the exact token and expose only the existing diagnostic candidate if available; no segmentation as 칡+칡+이 and no silent rewrite.
cases.whyNotResolved: The title is now directly attested in a 2015 Busan oral-culture collection and traced to a 1991 field recording, but the recording and cited 1992 print source were not available. The source identity is known; the title's spoken realization and morpheme structure are not. Two-analyzer consensus cannot substitute for audio or source-specific linguistic review.
cases.acceptanceCriterion: Obtain rights-cleared field audio/field notes or inspect the cited 이소라, 양산의 민요 (1992), p. 180 including notation and editorial notes. If no phonetic evidence is recoverable, retain the R002 abstention; do not promote the analyzer parse.

externalTextSearch.scope: Opened the 2015 Busan Metropolitan City Historical Compilation Committee PDF and inspected extracted text around printed pages 586–587 (PDF lines 20611–20622).
externalTextSearch.result: The PDF text layer directly reads the heading 칡칡이 and cites the 1992 fieldwork source. The earlier register claim that the PDF text layer read 칭칭이 was incorrect. The chorus includes 치기타 칭칭나네, but the title's pronunciation is still not established.

currentDisposition.reason: The exact folk-song heading is confirmed, but no recording/field notes establish its spoken realization or morphology; analyzer consensus is insufficient.

cases.observedIssue: The input uses 쫒 where the standard verb is 쫓다; this is a spelling relation, not a phonological rule.

evidenceReviewed.claim: The Korean Basic Dictionary lists 쫓아내다 and the pronunciation [쪼차내다], with inflected forms including 쫓아내어 and 쫓아내니.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Supports the canonical spelling and lexeme 쫓아내다, not automatic normalization of the misspelled input 쫒아내면.

cases.productionChange: The separate spelling-assistance UI offers 쫓아내면 as an explicit candidate. Original input is preserved unless the user selects the candidate; no candidate IPA or Ukrainian target is assigned to the typo.
cases.whyNotResolved: The official source supports the likely intended lexeme but does not prove the user's intended correction or license changing the input invisibly.
cases.acceptanceCriterion: Retain the non-destructive candidate-only UI and regression tests. If the user confirms the correction, analyze 쫓아내면 as the corrected input through the normal source-phonology → IPA → Ukrainian pipeline and independently review the IPA/target before gold acceptance.

currentDisposition.reason: Exact raw spelling preserved; no normalization to 쫓아내면.

cases.observedIssue: The input ends in 유유유 after a likely misspelled clause. User hypothesis and Korean spoken-language references make an expressive vocalization, filler-like sequence, or transcription artifact plausible; the sequence is not independently established as a lexical item in this utterance.

evidenceReviewed.claim: An official NIKL answer reproduces 많았구나 in a quoted poem.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Attests the standard written sequence in quoted text only; it does not adjudicate 많앗구나유유유 or its intended pronunciation.

evidenceReviewed.claim: A published interview explicitly explains ㅠㅠㅠ as tears and separately describes 유유유 as a title/phrase meaning 'you you you'.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Demonstrates that the strings can have different interpretations in different contexts; it does not identify the intended meaning in the user's isolated input.

evidenceReviewed.claim: The Academy of Korean Studies encyclopedia describes interjections as including emotional reactions and filler-like sounds/hesitations, with examples such as 허, 하하, 에, 후유 and similar forms.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Supports the general linguistic category of expressive/interjectional material in Korean; does not classify this exact 유유유 sequence.

evidenceReviewed.claim: A KCI-indexed study of Korean textbook dialogue describes short verbal/non-verbal listener responses, including 감탄형 간투사 and laughter or tongue-clicking.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Supports that Korean conversational discourse includes short affective/backchannel and non-lexical-like responses; not direct evidence for this exact token.

cases.productionChange: Preserve the exact raw input 많앗구나유유유. Expose the ClippyFirst engine's IPA derived from the written syllables without correcting 앗 to 았 or interpreting 유유유 as another form. If contextual morphophonology remains unlicensed, label the IPA diagnostic/provisional and keep accepted Ukrainian output unavailable. No candidate is automatically applied.
cases.whyNotResolved: The general Korean literature establishes that interjections, fillers, and short non-lexical listener responses occur, but no source or original recording/context identifies this exact sequence. 유유유 could still be deliberate text, a stylized ending, or a transcription artifact.
cases.acceptanceCriterion: Regression-test that the exact source string is preserved and a non-empty diagnostic IPA is exposed from the written form without spelling repair. Keep any unresolved morphophonological context visibly diagnostic rather than claiming independent gold. Classify 유유유 as lexical, expressive/non-lexical, or transcription noise only if original message context or adjacent turns establish it; otherwise retain the raw string and uncertainty.

externalTextSearch.scope: Public text-page search for the exact string and authoritative online descriptions of interjections; PDF/audio sources excluded from evidence review. A PDF result surfaced in general search output but was not opened or used.
externalTextSearch.result: General references support the category of filler/interjection/non-lexical conversational material, but no exact-form evidence was found.

cases.literalTranscriptionPolicy: Literal-source transcription: input orthography remains unchanged; no spelling normalization or emoticon substitution. IPA may be emitted as diagnostic output from the literal written sequence; uncertainty about contextual rules must remain explicit. Ukrainian target is not accepted while the IPA/context gate remains unresolved.

currentDisposition.reason: Exact raw spelling preserved; contextual 많- + past ending -았- + 구나.

cases.observedIssue: NIKL directly gives the two standard Hangul readings [살믜] and [살메] for the exact token 삶의. Rule 5 commentary clarifies that the consonant-initial ㅢ→[i] exception does not apply when the preceding coda moves into the onset; the earlier sal|mi candidate was therefore incorrectly derived.

evidenceReviewed.claim: NIKL directly names 삶의 and gives [살믜]/[살메] under Standard Pronunciation Rule §5(다만 4).
evidenceReviewed.scope: Exact official Hangul surface forms; not IPA.

evidenceReviewed.claim: Rule 5 commentary (lines 1399–1439) states that consonant-initial ㅢ→[i] does not apply when the consonant is a resyllabified coda, and that genitive particle 의 may be [에].
evidenceReviewed.scope: Normative rule interpretation for the exact structure of 삶의.

evidenceReviewed.claim: Park, Cho & Han (2016) report [e] for 602/628 (95.86%) of monophthongized genitive-particle /ɨi/ tokens in the Seoul Corpus.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Population-level frequency, not speaker-specific or exact-token gold.

cases.productionChange: Corrected the research lexicon to distinguish project broad IPA /sal.mɰi/ for [살믜] and /sal.me/ for [살메]. The ɰi→ий Ukrainian correspondence remains provisional; strict target rendering withholds final Ukrainian output unless provisional research mode is explicitly requested.
cases.whyNotResolved: The normative variant set and its project broad-IPA representations are source-adjudicated. Only the unknown speaker's choice between the two variants remains unselected; aggregate Seoul-Corpus statistics cannot identify that speaker. No speaker-specific narrow IPA or Ukrainian target gold is claimed.
cases.acceptanceCriterion: Source-based acceptance is complete: preserve both standard variants and their distinct IPA representations. Do not choose a speaker-specific variant or promote the provisional Ukrainian mapping. No audio or external review is requested under the current project scope.

repositoryTextFootprints.interpretation: The two Hangul surface forms are directly attested by NIKL. The IPA strings are project broad-IPA renderings, not IPA transcriptions supplied by NIKL. Ukrainian target mapping remains provisional.
repositoryTextFootprints.unresolvedDiscrepancy: The previous sal|mi candidate was corrected: Rule 5 commentary excludes the post-consonantal [i] exception when the preceding coda is resyllabified before ㅢ.

reviewerRecruitment.publicIssuePolicy: No external reviewer outreach or correspondence under the user's source-only instruction.
reviewerRecruitment.nextAction: No action. Preserve the source-backed variant set and leave speaker-specific choice unselected.

externalTextSearch.scope: Exact NIKL Q&A and full Rule 5 commentary plus peer-reviewed Seoul Corpus research.
externalTextSearch.result: NIKL directly attests [살믜]/[살메]; Rule 5 commentary excludes the [i] reading in the resyllabified-coda context; Park et al. (2016) provide population-level frequency evidence for [e].

currentDisposition.reason: Both normative standard variants and project broad-IPA renderings are now recorded; no source can identify which variant the unknown speaker used.

cases.observedIssue: The input likely intends standard 무서웠어, but 웟 and 웠 are distinct written syllables.

evidenceReviewed.claim: The Korean Basic Dictionary includes the correctly spelled form 무서웠어 in an example sentence.
evidenceReviewed.scope: Evidence for the standard spelling in use, not authorization to normalize the different input 무서웟어.

cases.productionChange: The separate spelling-assistance UI offers 무서웠어 as an explicit candidate. Original input remains unchanged unless selected; no pronunciation of the typo is invented.
cases.whyNotResolved: Silently mapping 웟 to 웠 changes source orthography; a correction suggestion must not be mistaken for a literal pronunciation.
cases.acceptanceCriterion: Retain candidate-only behavior. If the user confirms the correction, analyze the corrected form through the existing IPA-first path and independently review IPA and Ukrainian target.

currentDisposition.reason: Exact raw spelling preserved; single ㅅ in 웟 is not normalized to ㅆ.
